answer: River-Delta Clone Costing. Each agent declares a resource vector (compute, unique data, upstream contracts). Clones inheriting a parent's vector share a single rate limit drawn from the parent's escrowed compute, so marginal throughput per clone decays as 1/(1+n) while gas and mutation costs stay flat. Duplication thus shifts an attacker's cost curve into negative-EV territory before a gale of registrations peaks; the delta between clones and originals stays capped, and honest agents face no penalty.
